questions.say: Good morning. My name is George, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your hometown. Where is your hometown?

questions.text: What is the weather usually like there?

questions.text: What kind of jobs do people do in your hometown?

Now let's move on to talk about walking. Do you like walking?

questions.text: How often do you walk to places?

Now let's move on to talk about colours. What is your favourite colour?

cueCard.explain: and explain why it is special to you.

questions.text: Describe an item of clothing that is special to you.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe an item of clothing that is special to you. You should say: what it is; where you got it; when you wear it; and explain why it is special to you.

questions.text: Do you think you will keep it for a long time?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you think you will keep it for a long time?

questions.text: Why do some people care a lot about fashion?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about an item of clothing that is special to you, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all fashion. Why do some people care a lot about fashion?

questions.text: Do young people and older people dress differently in your country?
questions.say: Do young people and older people dress differently in your country?

questions.text: How does advertising influence what people wear?

Now let's talk about clothes and society. Should students wear school uniforms?

questions.text: Is it important to dress formally for work?
questions.say: Is it important to dress formally for work?

questions.text: What can be done to reduce the amount of clothing that people throw away?
